builders.angle: LITERAL. Work BRIEF-r13's three fix lists in order and exactly as written -- every item in them was named by two or three judges, and a candidate that simply clears all of them should win. Take the grafts the fix lists name, and nothing the fix lists do not ask for. The contracts in BRIEF-r12 bind every change: re-photograph the coach at three steps, not one, so the new pointer and spotlight are proven against more than one target.

ONE SYSTEM OUT OF THREE CANDIDATES. Round 12's judges named grafts from all three builders -- ORMOLU's Marmalade cameo and fleur-de-lis finial for the coach, ORMOLU's ribbon for the toast, GESSO's medal on a silk ribbon and its theatre valance, VELLUM's shelf of skull, books and candle and its moon and paw medallions for the veil. Read those branches (git show ui/r12-chrome-{a,b,c}:<path>) and bring the named ideas into the merged pieces so the three read as ONE family of objects -- the same cartouche, the same rule, the same metal -- rather than three builders' vocabularies side by side. Port any asset you need into tools/prep_chrome.py; do not add a second script.

LIGHT AND OBJECT. The judges' deepest complaint about all three pieces is that they are drawn, not lit: a spotlight that is a rectangle, a veil whose moonlit house has no candle to answer it, a medal that is a flat vector star. Lead with light and with the physical object: the coach's target stands in a pool of candlelight that falls off into the room, with filigree at its corners only; the veil gets real candlelight -- a lantern beside the portraits, candles in the lower corners -- and heavy framed portraits on a backing plate; the toast's medal is an engraved, lit object hung on a ribbon, its metal the tier. Every light must be a candle or the moon, never a CSS glow; judges have marked box-shadow glows down in every round.
